newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to keep close ties with Iran - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia to keep close ties with Iran - agency.

text.p: Russia has told Iran that ties between Moscow and Tehran will not be affected by the latter's row with the West, Itar-Tass news agency said on Sunday.

"Russia is firmly committed to friendly relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Tass quoted Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov's message to Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati as saying.

Tass said in a report from Tehran that the Russian ambassador in Iran, Sergei Tretyakov, had delivered the message to Velayati earlier on Sunday. Foreign ministry in Moscow could not immediately confirm Tass report.

"The recent events...will not effect our Russian-Iranian relations," the message said, referring to the row over a German court verdict that accused Tehran leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. Iran has denied involvement.
"During our conversation, Velayati praised bilateral relation and pointed out common views shared by the two countries on a series of international issues," Tass quoted Tretyakov as saying.

The European Union withdrew its ambassadors after the April 10 German court verdict. A meeting of EU foreign ministers last week week agreed to send the envoys back but suspended ministerial contacts.
Iran's foreign ministry has said it was suspending all talks with the EU, including those affecting human rights, terrorism and chemical and nuclear weapons.

Russia, deeply unhappy about a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation decision to grant membership to some eastern European countries, has made clear it was looking for ways to diversify its foreign policy after the western-dominated first post-Soviet years.
Russian officials have singled out Iran, along with China and India, among the new partners.
